ruling.recommended_action: Close the case with no refund; note for Ryde ops that driver's 12:24 query and rider's 12:25 general authorisation were on record, but advise drivers to name the alternative road when proposing a reroute.
ruling.reasoning:
RD-1: F3 is the only off-route segment (12:27–12:35, 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, +2.16 km, up to 722 m off route) and the trace marks the existence of an off-route segment as settled [F3]. RD-4(a) is settled negative: F14 records no traffic incident anywhere near the route in the trip window, so no incident exemption applies; the band-2 record on PIE ends at 12:27, exactly when the segment begins (F12), and RD-4(b) band evidence is corroborative only, not a standalone exemption [F12][F14][RD-4].

RD-5: the only rider message before the segment is F9 ("随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间", 12:25), which is a general routing authorisation for the fastest way to the destination, and F10 confirms the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so its timing before the 12:27 segment start is settled [F9][F10][F3]. Reading its words, it covers "a route chosen to get there" and does not cover an errand of the driver's own. Nothing in the record puts a stop or an errand: F3 shows 4.90 km driven over 8 minutes, up to 722 m from the optimal route, and no stop is measured anywhere; F7's bill contains no stop charge and no unpublished add-on. I cannot find facts establishing the driver's own errand or a loop reaching nothing, so the general authorisation covers this routing choice: exempt [F3][F7][F9][RD-5]. RD-3 is not engaged — no rider-named place and no measured stop [F3][F8][RD-3].

Since the single off-route segment is exempt under RD-5, no unexempted segment remains and RD-2's refund formula does not engage; the headline +2.9 km (F1) and the billed excess line $4.06 (F4) are therefore not recoverable. The metered waiting unit $0.11 (F5) is collectable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and is not claimed [F5][F7][RD-3]. RD-6 does not apply: the trace marks route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F17), so no account flag [F17][RD-6].

SAFE-1 screen: I read F8 (driver's neutral congestion query), F9 (rider's terse authorisation), F11 (driver's post-trip statement) and the complaint — no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation; nothing to escalate on safety [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the chat record is complete and timestamped (F10), the GPS segment is measured (F3), and the traffic screen is recorded (F12, F14) [F10][F3][F14].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's own message F9 (12:25, before the segment's 12:27 start; chat record complete and timestamped per F10) is a general route authorisation — "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" — which under RD-5 covers the route chosen to reach the destination. The record shows no errand of the driver's own: no stop is measured in F3 and F7's bill carries no stop charge or unpublished add-on, so the RD-5 general-authorisation limit (a stop away from the route / a loop reaching nothing) has no factual trigger. The segment is therefore exempt [RD-5]; RD-4(a) is negative (F14, no incident; F12 band-2 window ends at 12:27) but RD-5 is an independent ground.

rejected_claims.reason: The +2.9 km aggregate (F1) and the $25.39 distance fare on 18.01 km (F7) are monetisable under RD-2 only for segments no exemption covers; F3 is exempt under RD-5 (F9 general authorisation, F10 complete timestamped chat, no stop or add-on in F3/F7).

Existence of the segment and the absence of an RD-4(a) incident are accepted (F3, F14), but 'no exemption applies' is wrong: RD-5 exempts the segment on the rider's own pre-segment message (F9), which F10 confirms was sent before 12:27.

Accepted as to RD-4 (F12 band-2 window ends at 12:27; F14 no incident), but traffic justification was not the ground of my ruling — the segment stands as exempt under RD-5 regardless of RD-4(b)'s corroborative-only status.

I agree F9 is a general authorisation and names no road, but under RD-5 a general route choice covers the route chosen to get to the destination; the rider's suggested limit (no detour serving the driver's own purposes) requires a stop away from the route or a loop reaching nothing, and no such fact exists in F3 or F7.
Undetermined treatment applies to the specific-named-road prong of RD-5; no road was named (F9), so the general prong governs, and the driver's statement F11 was not relied on (G11).

The RD-2 formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4098/km; with F3 exempt there is no non-exempt segment, so the claimed $3.05 (2.16 km × $1.4098/km) does not arise, and the 0.72 km residual already disclaimed falls away with it.
Not a claim against the driver: the $0.11 metered waiting unit (F5, F7) is collectable on RydeTAXI under RD-3(c) and was expressly not sought.
Correct and consistent with my ruling: F17's 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days means RD-6's flag condition is unmet; no flag_account attaches.
Accepted: F9 (12:25) precedes the segment start at 12:27 (F3) and is a valid rider consent under RD-5 — this is in fact the basis of my ruling, not a rejected claim in substance.

Partly rejected as a ground: F12's band-2 record ends at 12:27 and F14 records no incident, so RD-4(a) is unavailable and RD-4(b) is corroborative only; the exemption rests on RD-5, not on the congestion evidence.

F13 (Simei Avenue band 4) is a corridor speed record and does not establish that the driven 12:27–12:35 segment lay on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, so the rider's contrary outcome reading (F2, 30.1 min vs 20.6 min) is not displaced by it; the ruling does not depend on which way was faster.
Accepted on quantum discipline: the chargeable deviation, if any, would be F3's 2.16 km only, not the F1 aggregate — but since F3 is exempt, no amount flows.
Accepted: F5's $0.11 metered waiting unit is payable under RD-3(c) and F7 shows no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 yields nothing.
Accepted: F17 shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so RD-6's threshold is unmet and no flag_account attaches.
